title: Randomized Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis
formal: For every \(\varepsilon >0\) some clause width k precludes randomized \(O(2^{(1- \varepsilon )n})\) time for k-SAT.

sentences: Randomized SETH asks whether bounded-width satisfiability resists every uniform fixed saving in the exhaustive-search exponent.
For each positive \(\varepsilon\), the conjecture requires some fixed width k with no randomized \(O(2^{(1- \varepsilon )n})\) algorithm.
The width may grow as the demanded saving shrinks, so fast algorithms at individual small widths remain compatible.
This randomized version supports lower bounds that must exclude randomized algorithms for their target tasks.
The saved textbook note does not spell out error and polynomial input-length factors, and deterministic SETH alone cannot silently supply the stronger randomized exclusion.
